newsitem.title: USA: Africa-bound U.S. troops not armed for combat: Perry.
newsitem.headline: Africa-bound U.S. troops not armed for combat: Perry.

text.p: Defense Secretary William Perry said on Thursday that Africa-bound U.S. troops would be armed to protect themselves but not to conduct combat operations while helping to deliver aid to Rwandan refugees.

Perry told reporters the projected ground force of as many as 1,000 U.S. troops, which will be part of a Canadian-led multinational expedition, would have "robust" rules of engagement to protect themselves.

"We will have arms and have what we call robust rules of engagement to allow our forces to protect themselves" in the volatile region along the Rwanda-Zaire border, Perry said. Up to 1.5 million refugees are in dire need of food, water and shelter in the area, relief workers said.
Perry spoke during a picture-taking session with visiting Defence Minister Severin Adjori of the West African state of Benin.

The White House said on Wednesday that President Bill Clinton had decided in principle to send U.S. troops and helicopters, provided the mission was of a limited duration and involved other countries' forces as well.

About 1.5 million refugees, mainly Hutus, fled Rwanda in 1994, fearing reprisals after the massacre of up to a million Tutsis and Hutu moderates. The eastern Zairean province of Kivu has remained politically tense since then, with a new war breaking out in September between Tutsi residents of Zaire and local Zairians backed by Zaire's rag-tag army.
